before.description: Verify that a buyer can add one eligible order item from My Orders to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet, including NFC tickets that use the authenticated Google Wallet flow.
before.preconditions:
A buyer has an order with exactly one eligible item that exposes digital wallet passes.
The item is activated, paid or usable, not transferred, not listed for resale, and has barcode/pass data available.
For NFC Google Wallet coverage, the buyer is logged in and the order contains one eligible NFC pass-only ticket.
Use a compatible OS/browser for the wallet type being tested.
before.postconditions: The pass is available in the native wallet and the order item remains accessible from My Orders.

steps.action: Open My Orders and select an order with exactly one eligible wallet item.
steps.expected_result: The order details page loads for the selected order.

steps.action: Verify the Add to Wallet action for the detected wallet provider.
steps.expected_result: The Apple Wallet or Google Wallet action is visible and enabled for the item. For logged-in NFC Google Wallet coverage, the Google Wallet action is available from order details.

steps.action: Click the Add to Wallet action.
steps.expected_result: The platform wallet save flow opens without a Showpass UI error.

steps.action: When running the NFC Google Wallet variant, observe the redirected Google Wallet save flow.
steps.expected_result: The Google Wallet save page or provider flow opens with expected pass data and no Showpass UI error.

steps.action: Complete or simulate the provider flow to save the pass.
steps.expected_result: The pass is saved to the native wallet or provider confirmation page.

steps.action: Open the saved pass and review the pass details.
steps.expected_result: The event, item, date/time, venue, ticket holder, and seat details are accurate for the order item.

after.description:
Add one eligible item to the phone’s actual wallet and verify its saved branding and identity. Run every ItemType with each OS: eight runs. Ticket with both OS values and NFCTicket with both OS values preserve the ordinary/NFC and iOS/Android selections from the existing branding lifecycle case. A provider confirmation or sample page preview is not an installed-pass result.

| ItemType | Item required |
| --- | --- |
| Ticket | One paid, unused ticket for a future event with ordinary barcode delivery |
| Product | One paid, unused product item eligible for digital wallet delivery |
| Memberships | One active membership eligible for digital wallet delivery |
| NFCTicket | One paid, unused NFC-only event ticket; NFC means phone tap admission rather than a static barcode |

| OS | Device and expected organization branding |
| --- | --- |
| iOS | A supported iPhone with Apple Wallet; background, foreground and label colors plus the configured Apple logo and strip in the supported pass layout |
| Android | A supported Android phone with Google Wallet; configured background color and Google Wallet logo, with the configured strip where the pass layout displays it |

| Platform | View |
| --- | --- |
| WebPublic | Mobile |

Use at least one event run with different phone and event timezones. Record both zones and the expected event-local date/time before adding the pass. Record OS version and Apple layout switch state; advanced iOS 18 image placement is a separate physical-device check.
after.preconditions:
* The customer owns an order containing exactly one selected eligible item. It is usable, has pass data available, and has not been transferred or listed for resale.
* The customer is signed into My Orders on the selected phone and can complete the real provider Add flow.
* An employee with Manage Events and Manage Organization Info has saved an organization design containing recognizable Apple and Google logos, a strip and distinct recorded colors. Use an organization reserved for these branding checks, without affected real customer passes.
* An administrator confirms the selected item inherits the organization’s design: no separate design is assigned to its event/ticket type, product/variant, or membership group/level.
* For NFCTicket, the organization setting enable_use_nfc_ticket is on, enable_order_barcode is off, and the event was set to is_nfc_pass_only before its tickets were sold. These are saved settings, not a page visibility flag.
* The selected item is not already installed in the phone’s wallet. Record its identity, displayed date/time and seat where relevant, plus the saved branding expected for the chosen OS.
after.postconditions:
* Retain the order and evidence; remove only this run’s installed pass from the controlled phone after recording the result.
* Restore any organization branding changed solely for this run and reopen the form to confirm restoration.

steps.action: As the customer, open My Orders and choose the order containing the selected item.
steps.expected_result: The correct order and its one eligible item appear.

steps.action: Select Add to Apple Wallet or Add to Google Wallet for that item.
steps.data: Use the provider for the selected OS.
steps.expected_result: The correct provider’s save flow opens with that item’s details; NFC Google Wallet access uses the signed-in customer’s flow.

steps.action: Complete the provider’s Add action.
steps.expected_result: The item is saved in the phone’s actual wallet.

steps.action: Open the saved item in Apple Wallet or Google Wallet.
steps.expected_result: The item shows the recorded organization colors and provider-specific branding for the selected OS, rather than another organization’s or an older design.

steps.action: Compare the pass details with the purchased item.
steps.data: Recorded item, date/time and seat where relevant.
steps.expected_result: Identity and date/time match the item; a selected NFC-only ticket does not expose a static entry barcode.

steps.action: Return to My Orders and reopen the order.
steps.expected_result: The original item remains accessible; one intended pass has been saved for it.
